Listing form changes need IT approval → start with a paper sticker if needed.
pearls: Agree with consultants which conditions justify early surgery before cycle 1.
Show how many children resolved while waiting; it supports the rule.
Recruit the waiting-list manager to enforce the fields.

pitfalls: PET capacity is regional → share the data with the PET provider early.
Scans booked early to 'catch' recurrence → quote the false-positive risk.
Small numbers → use a 12-month look-back across the network.
Last fraction date hard to find → take it from the radiotherapy system.
pearls: Recruit a head and neck oncologist and the MDT coordinator.
Report equivocal scans by timing; early scans often cause them.
Keep the same date rule in both cycles.

pitfalls: Status recorded at diagnosis but not updated → capture the status on the day of diagnosis.
Clinicians feel it adds distress at bad news → allow referral within 2 weeks via the CNS.
Stop-smoking service capacity → agree the referral route before cycle 1.
Former smokers counted as smokers → define 'current' as smoked in the last month.
pearls: Recruit the head and neck CNS team and the Trust tobacco dependency lead.
Opt-out wording lifts uptake more than asking.
Measure quit status at treatment start as an outcome.

pitfalls: Dietitian not present at MDT → allow a dietetic clinic entry before treatment to count.
Decision recorded only as 'dietitian to see' → define that as a fail.
Mixed OMFS and ENT pathways → include both and report by team.
Unplanned tube counts are small → report them descriptively.
pearls: Recruit the head and neck dietitian as co-lead.
Agree the three allowed decisions before cycle 1.
Record weight at diagnosis; it strengthens the case for the field.

pitfalls: No nuclear medicine or sentinel node pathway locally → treat this as a service gap and escalate.
Small numbers → use 24 months and all network sites.
Surgeons prefer neck dissection → the reason box keeps choice visible and discussable.
Staging changes on pathology → classify by clinical stage at MDT.
pearls: Recruit the OMFS head and neck lead and nuclear medicine.
Report morbidity (shoulder, length of stay) alongside the rate.
Agree the cervical access exception wording first.

pitfalls: Surgeons cite reasons outside TA1 (e.g. distal caries risk in the second molar) → record these as 'other' and discuss them rather than failing silently.
Indication in the referral but not the letter → accept any pre-operative OMFS document.
Mixed operators (dental core trainees, staff grades) → report by grade to target teaching.
The form becomes a tick-box habit → spot-check 10 notes against radiographs.
pearls: Recruit the OMFS clinical lead and the day-surgery booking team.
Agree how to classify 'other' reasons before cycle 1.
Include pericoronitis episode counts; they are the most common grey area.

pitfalls: Tests ordered by GPs are invisible → check the shared pathology system.
Split care between dermatology and plastics → include both and report by team.
Low results not acted on → add supplementation advice as a secondary field.
Laboratory rejects 'non-standard' requests → confirm the test code first.
pearls: Recruit the skin cancer CNS; they run results clinics.
Use the diagnosis date from histology to avoid disputes.
Share the result template with GPs for follow-up.

pitfalls: TBSA not recorded, so eligibility unclear → report 'TBSA missing' separately and count as unassessable.
Coding misses burns → add a free-text search for 'burn' and 'scald'.
Paediatric burns go to a different ED → include both or state the scope.
Referrals by phone leave no record → ask the burns service for its referral log.
pearls: Recruit an ED consultant and the burns network outreach nurse.
Use the network's own referral portal data for cross-checking.
Measure Lund and Browder use; it drives correct TBSA.

pitfalls: ED already gave vaccine but did not record status → check ED administration records.
Status unknown in adults → Table 4 treats uncertain status as not adequately primed; teach that rule.
Immunoglobulin supply → confirm the local HNIG/IM-TIG product and route first.
Guidance updates between cycles → use the same version for both cycles and note the date.
pearls: Recruit the hand trauma nurse lead and ED pharmacist.
Print Table 4 on the back of the proforma.
Use the GP summary care record to confirm status quickly.

pitfalls: Theatre washout delays the review → a documented 'continue IV until washout' counts as review.
Paper charts hide times → take times from the administration record.
Small numbers in summer-heavy seasonality → use 6 months.
Stop dates overridden → audit overrides in cycle 2.
pearls: Recruit the antimicrobial pharmacist.
Report length of stay and IV days as balancing measures.
Agree first dose time as the clock start.

pitfalls: Surgeons keep day-1 reviews for reassurance → show unplanned attendance rates as a safety measure.
Complications coded late → use the operation record, not coding.
Some day-1 visits are for trainee cases → decide before cycle 1 if these are allowed.
Telephone calls not recorded → add a phone-call field to the nurse template.
pearls: Recruit the cataract lead and the outpatient booking manager.
Report clinic slots freed; managers support it.
Track unplanned attendance to reassure consultants.

pitfalls: Laser capacity limits offers → record capacity delays separately.
Severity grading varies → use the Hodapp or local staging agreed in advance.
Offers made verbally are unrecorded → template field fixes this.
Optometrist-led clinics use different letters → update all templates.
pearls: Recruit the glaucoma lead and laser nurse.
Report acceptance rates to plan laser sessions.
Include both consultant and optometrist clinics.

pitfalls: Referral receipt date not recorded → use the e-referral timestamp.
Injector capacity (nurse injectors) → plan staffing before the change.
Patient-choice delays counted as fails → record them separately.
Second-eye conversions dilute the sample → exclude them.
pearls: Recruit the medical retina lead and nurse injector lead.
Report median days as well as the 14-day rate.
Triage referrals daily, including Fridays.

pitfalls: Paper charts hide exact times → use e-obs timestamps or accept charted times.
Patients spread over many wards → take the case list from the head injury admission code.
Nursing staff feel blamed → present with nursing leads and focus on the system.
Frequency resets after deterioration are complex → record deterioration and schedule reset as notes.
pearls: Co-lead with a ward nurse manager.
Agree the 15-minute tolerance before cycle 1.
Show missed deterioration cases (anonymised) to motivate.
